"AVATAR: THE FOUR ELEMENTS

2D Open-World RPG Adventure

Create a large-scale 2D open-world RPG based on Avatar: The Last Airbender. The game should allow the player to live in the Avatar universe, explore its world, develop elemental abilities, meet characters, discover secrets, and create their own destiny.

1. Character Creation and Birth

The game begins with the player being born into the world.

Every new game should randomly determine:

- Your nation of origin.
- Your family and social background.
- Whether you are a bender or a non-bender.
- Your elemental bending ability, if you are a bender.
- Your starting attributes and personality traits.

You can be born into one of the four nations:

- Water Tribe.
- Earth Kingdom.
- Fire Nation.
- Air Nomads.

There is also a rare possibility of being born as the Avatar.

Being the Avatar should be extremely rare. If you are born as the Avatar, you can eventually master all four elements: Water, Earth, Fire, and Air.

If you are not the Avatar, you can still become an incredibly powerful bender.

2. Elemental Bending System

If your character is a bender, you should be able to learn and develop your element.

Each element must have a large variety of abilities, techniques, animations, and combat styles.

Waterbending:

- Water whips.
- Water blades.
- Ice spikes.
- Ice walls.
- Healing.
- Water waves.
- Bloodbending (extremely advanced and rare).
- Plantbending.

Earthbending:

- Earth walls.
- Rock projectiles.
- Earth pillars.
- Seismic sense.
- Sandbending.
- Metalbending.
- Lava bending (extremely rare).

Firebending:

- Fireballs.
- Fire streams.
- Fire walls.
- Lightning generation.
- Lightning redirection.
- Advanced fire techniques.

Airbending:

- Air blasts.
- Air shields.
- Air jumps.
- Air spheres.
- Tornadoes.
- Air scooters.
- Flight (advanced technique).

Each element should have its own skill tree, progression system, and unique animations.

Non-benders should also have their own combat abilities, weapons, equipment, and fighting styles.

3. The Avatar Mode

If you are born as the Avatar, you will have access to a special progression system.

You must learn all four elements, find teachers, train, and gradually unlock your Avatar abilities.

Features:

- Avatar State.
- Access to all four elements.
- Special Avatar techniques.
- Enhanced speed and strength.
- Powerful elemental combinations.
- Connection with previous Avatars.
- Spiritual training.

The Avatar State should be incredibly powerful, with unique visual effects, animations, and sound effects.

However, controlling the Avatar State should require training.

4. Open World

Create a huge interconnected 2D world with different regions, cities, villages, temples, forests, mountains, oceans, deserts, and hidden locations.

The player should be able to freely explore the world.

Include locations such as:

- Ba Sing Se.
- Omashu.
- Southern Water Tribe.
- Northern Water Tribe.
- Fire Nation Capital.
- Air Temples.
- Kyoshi Island.
- Ember Island.
- Swamps.
- Hidden caves.
- Ancient ruins.

Every location should have NPCs, activities, secrets, shops, quests, and unique environments.

The world should feel alive, with NPCs following daily routines, interacting with each other, and reacting to the player's actions.

5. The Spirit World

The Spirit World should be a separate explorable dimension.

The player should be able to enter it through spiritual portals, special locations, or meditation.

Include:

- Unique spirit creatures.
- Ancient spirits.
- Dangerous areas.
- Spirit forests.
- Mysterious temples.
- Spiritual quests.
- Rare spiritual abilities.
- Connections between the physical and spiritual worlds.

Some spirits should be friendly, while others may attack the player.

Include important spirits such as the Ocean Spirit, Moon Spirit, Hei Bai, and other creatures inspired by the Avatar universe.

6. Character Progression

The player should grow older and become stronger over time.

Include:

- Characte

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
